glosses: A narrow ledge or shelf, as along the top or bottom of a slope.
A raised bank or path, especially the bank of a canal opposite the towpath.

examples.text: The big canals in Europe, in Holland, have a great big berm on the side of the canal several feet wide, which they leave there on purpose to plant reeds in, so as to get a reedy vegetation to protect their slope. Then, beyond that, there is an earthen slope that is grassed and sodded.

glosses: One of the flat terraces on the slope of an open-pit mine.
A terrace or shelf of sand along a beach, formed above the high tide water level by wave action.

examples.text: On some beaches, the berm grows higher in summer and flattens out in the rougher winter seas.

glosses: A long mound or bank of earth, used especially as a barrier or to provide insulation.

examples.text: A berm separates the Moroccan-controlled and Polisario-controlled parts of Western Sahara.

glosses: A small wall along the edge of a bench of an open-pit mine, intended to prevent items falling over the crest.
A ledge between the parapet and the moat in a fortification.
A strip of land between a street and sidewalk.

examples.text: The sun soaked our street in hot yellow, and the berms were gasping for water.

glosses: The edge of a road.
